newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares steady in weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares steady in weak demand.

text.p: Jordanian shares were steady on Monday with weak demand as investors took a break from the aggressive buying which boosted stocks last week, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.03 percent to close at 157.17 points in low turnover of 749,748 dinars ($1,105,896).
Although on Sunday the market began to reverse an upward trend which sent stocks to 14-month highs last week, it is still close to its highest levels for over a year.
Brokers say a spate of select foreign buying has helped boost prices since parliament abolished two weeks ago a punitive 15 percent tax on companies which raise capital with transfers from reserves.

"There market has begun to retreat since yesterday with fewer purchase orders, but there is no selling pressure... investors are awaiting 1996 corporate earnings," said Ibrahim Odeh, a broker in al-Wataniyeh for Financial Services.
Odeh said foreign and institutional investors were taking a pause but he expected they would resume active buying on select blue chips.
One of the stocks which has seen active institutional and foreign buying, Arab Pharmaceutical Chemicals, shed 0.03 dinars to 1.57 dinars.
Heavily weighted Arab Bank which was the busiest stock, fell 1.00 dinars to 261 in 151,620 dinars worth of trade.
The second busiest stock, and one of the few gainers, Arab Potash, rose 0.09 dinars to 6.10 in trade worth 74,538 dinars.
Overall shares in 29 companies fell, six rose, and another ten traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange shed 0.23 percent to 83.06 points.
